overview.headline: United States doubled in size with 1803 Louisiana Purchase from France for $15 million

keyPoints.point: The United States purchased land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million in the transaction with France
keyPoints.quote: the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million

keyPoints.point: Negotiators Livingston and Monroe were authorized to pay up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas
keyPoints.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas

keyPoints.point: President Jefferson as a generally strict interpreter of the Constitution wondered if the Government was authorized to acquire new territory
keyPoints.quote: who wondered if the U.S. Government (and especially the President) was authorized to acquire new territory

keyPoints.point: Desire to maintain balance between free states and slave states required fragile compromises as sectional weaknesses grew over slavery
keyPoints.quote: the desire to maintain a balance between "free states" and "slave states" required a series of fragile compromises

keyTerms.quote: The Louisiana Purchase was the first major cession of land in a long series of expansions that span the 19th century.

keyTerms.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery
